bitstream_source: main 81630972 by the bench's nightly job (icepi/build/v1.3.bit)
firmware_sha256: of each python/bench_firmware.py entry as sorted, compact JSON, or of the test/ file, at the run's commit
bench: an Icepi Zero (ECP5 LFE5U-25F) running the chip at 48 MHz on bench carrier v1.2, Pico A as the host on SPI, nothing, Pico B idle on OUT0, analyser A (fx2lafw) at 24 MS/s
scope: the bytes on the wire and their timing in one run of spdif_ac3, as the analyser saw them
limits: one run of one board, the ECP5 build of the chip's RTL, not the ASIC
the run's files are the bench's own record, tied together by SHA256SUMS, and CI derives the decode and the timing from the capture alone
each edge is known to a sample either way and the analyser's crystal to 100 ppm, and a window the capture cannot settle is unresolved, not passed
the bitstream is named by its sha256, and its netlist's, built from main 81630972 by the bench's nightly job (icepi/build/v1.3.bit) by the bench's notes, which CI does not rebuild
our own demo on the held-out S/PDIF firmware, not a drawn or sealed protocol, sending one AC-3 frame in an IEC 61937 burst that FFmpeg made
sigrok's spdif reads nothing past the line's low from reset and misreads the burst when started after it, so its decode is not judged
demo/ffmpeg_referee.py reads the words by run length, and FFmpeg's spdif demuxer must find the frame sent in them
FFmpeg holds the frame's bytes, not the line code
the capture holds fewer frames than a 192-frame block, so the block's windows hold 192 times their mean
a half slot is about four samples, so its windows can stay unresolved
